newsitem.title: FINLAND: RAISIO TO COOPERATE WITH J&J CO ON BENECOL.
newsitem.headline: RAISIO TO COOPERATE WITH J&J CO ON BENECOL.

text.p: Finnish food group Raision Tehtaat said on Tuesday it had agreed to cooperate with McNeil Consumer Products, a Johnson & Johnson company, on the key ingredient for its Benecol margarine in North America.

"Raisio Group has signed a licensing agreement with McNeil Consumer Products, a Johnson & Johnson company, giving McNeil sole rights to the use of Raisio's Benecol stanol ester in a variety of forms to be introduced to the North American market," Raisio said in a statement.
Raisio said it was very satisfied with the deal.
"We predict that its long-term impact will be very favourable on Raisio Group's financial performance," CEO Matti Salminen said in the statement.
"The aim is to launch Benecol products on the U.S. market during spring 1998," it added.
The agreement with McNeil would enter force after it has received approval from U.S. competition authorities, it said.

Stanol ester, derived from plant sterol, is the key ingredient of Raisio's Benecol margarine and it has been proven to lower cholesterol levels in blood. Raisio Group holds patents for both the manufacture of stanol ester and the technology related to its use in foodstuffs.

Raisio markets the active ingredient in margarine in Finland, but it has stressed that its key feature is its fat-solubility, which means it can be delivered in different ways to appeal to the dietary tastes of different countries.
It said it plans to construct a stanol ester production plant in the U.S. and a pre-engineering study is already underway.
McNeil's know-how in medicine and its knowledge of the consumer market was important for launching Benecol stanol ester products on the North American market, it said.
Raisio said the size of the Finnish Benecol market was 90 million markka per year, noting that the U.S. has a population some 70 times Finland's five million population.
